hints: Notice the reagents, alkaline aqueous iodine is the classic test for one very specific group in a carbonyl compound.
Draw out 3-methylbutan-2-one as $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$ and spot the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ methyl ketone unit.
Remember the $\text{CH}_3$ next to the $\text{C=O}$ is lost as triiodomethane, so the carboxylate left behind has one carbon fewer than the starting ketone.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the iodoform reaction**

This is not simple oxidation. Alkaline aqueous iodine means the triiodomethane (iodoform) reaction for methyl ketones.

General rule:
$$\text{R-CO-CH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^- + \text{CHI}_3 + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Draw the starting ketone**

3-methylbutanone must be 3-methylbutan-2-one to be a ketone, with structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$.

It clearly contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so it will give a positive iodoform test.

**Identify the R group left behind**

Split the molecule at the carbonyl. The $\text{COCH}_3$ part becomes $\text{CHI}_3$.

The rest is $\text{R} = \text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$, an isopropyl group, which becomes $\text{R-COO}^-$ in alkali.

**Account for acidification**

Acidifying converts the carboxylate salt into the free carboxylic acid:
$$\text{R-COO}^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{R-COOH}$$
So we get $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH}$, which is 2-methylpropanoic acid, named here as methylpropanoic acid.

options.A: Incorrect. 3-methylbutanoic acid has 5 carbons, the same number as the starting ketone. The iodoform reaction always removes the methyl carbon as $\text{CHI}_3$, so the acid product must be one carbon shorter.
options.B: Incorrect. Butanoic acid is a straight-chain $\text{C}_4$ acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. Our R group is branched, $\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$, so the product must be branched, not straight-chain.
options.C: Correct. The $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ fragment is lost as $\text{CHI}_3$ and the remaining $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-$ group becomes $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOO}^-$, which on acidification gives $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH}$, methylpropanoic acid.
options.D: Incorrect. Propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, would come from butan-2-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$. Our ketone has an extra methyl branch on carbon 3, giving a branched $\text{C}_4$ acid instead.
